date: 2026-10-04

I consider writing recommendation letters a very important part of my job. I believe that if you participated in my courses and did well, then I owe you a recommendation letter. By writing you a letter I am not doing you a favor; I'm simply fulfilling my duties and rewarding you appropriately for your efforts.

Having said that, I will only write you a letter if I believe that your performance and participation in my class(es) were worth commending. I will not write a letter for you if I do not think I can write you a strong one.

If you found this page on my website, please send me a brief email first to ask whether I can write you a letter. If I've emailed you this page, then I'm interested in (**but haven't yet fully agreed to**) writing one.

Writing a strong recommendation letter takes significant time and effort. To help me write the best possible letter for you, I need you to do your part. Please follow the instructions below carefully; I cannot begin working on your letter until I receive all the requested information.

## Criteria

Here are the rough criteria I use when deciding whether to write a letter, by type of program:

| Program | Grade in my course | What else I look for | Will I write one? |
|:------|:------|:----------|:------|
| JHU AMS Combined Masters | Good | That you have kept taking interesting math classes | Yes; a brief letter, internal to the department |
| Summer internships, REUs, etc. | Matters less | Work ethic, office hours, problem solving, persistence | Yes, if you were engaged in my course |
| PhD programs and jobs | Good, but not enough | Genuine interest, and doing more than what is typically expected | Only if you were **exceptional**[^exceptional] |
| Non-JHU Masters | n/a | n/a | Usually not, but I'm happy to be a reference[^reference] |

[^exceptional]: Exceptional does not mean being at the top of the class. It means demonstrating genuine interest and doing more than what is typically expected.

[^reference]: I do not think there is anything useful I can add to a letter that is not already in your transcript, but I'm happy to answer an email or a phone call from the program.

## Documents to Send

At least a **month before the first deadline**, send me every document tied to your application, all in one email with the subject line "Recommendation letter: *your name*". This includes:

- A photo (please do not assume that I'll remember your name after two years)
- Which of my courses you took, and in which term
- Your final grade in each of my courses
- CV
- Unofficial transcript
- (Draft) statement of purpose
- Other work related to the program you're applying to, or to my courses

If you're applying to PhD programs, also share a Google Sheet or Excel spreadsheet listing every program, its deadline, how it collects letters (e.g. MathPrograms.org, a portal link, direct email), and a column for me to check off when I've submitted.

Please also tell me what you'd like me to highlight in your letter. Do not be modest or shy. Be clear, upfront and **advocate for yourself**; err on the side of claiming too much. I will use this as starting material for my letter. If I do not agree with anything you say, I'll simply leave it out, so you should not feel uncomfortable about blowing your own trumpet. But if you do not remind me of something important, I might fail to add it to the letter.

## What Happens Next

Once I have everything, I'll confirm whether I can write your letter. Please send me a reminder email about a week before each deadline, with the subject line "Recommendation letter reminder: *your name*, due *date*".
